title: 3D Snapshot
content: **List of Contents** Single View Multi View Save 3D window snapshots from one or more angles as images. 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Snapshot ▶ **3D Window (F10)** 2. Enter desired file name and location, then click **Save**. 3. Set details as needed: #### **Single View** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Image** **Size** | **Preset** | Customize or select from provided preset options. **Orientation** | Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Sets the unit of measurement for the image. **Resolution** | Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. **Colorway**** ** | ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44189528036633) Set whether to save only the current colorway or all colorways. Or, choose specific colorways by clicking the ![Select Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44191274180633) **Select Colorways** button. **Option** | **Transparent Background** | Save the image with a transparent background. **Save HTML File ** | A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. **Reset** | Resets the options back to the program default settings. #### **Multiview** **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Preview** | **Preset** | Mouse-over on the preview image ▶ Select desired view option from drop-down menu. **Custom** | Customize view angle in the 3D window. Mouse-over on the preview image ▶ Click on the camera icon. **Layout** | **View Count** | Select the number of views to capture. Set it up to 10 views. (ver 5.2) **Layout** | Select from horizontal/vertical/box layout options. **Single ****Image ****Size** | **Preset** | Customize or select from preset image size. **Orientation** | Select from portrait or landscape orientation options. **Width** | Set the width of the image. **Height** | Set the height of the image. **Unit** | Sets the unit of measurement for the image. **Resolution** | Sets the pixels per inch for the image. From ver3.2.0, the image resolution (ppi) will automatically adjust depending on the selected paper size for optimal printing results. **Colorway** | ![Update.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44189528036633) Set whether to save only the current colorway or all colorways. Or, choose specific colorways by clicking the ![Select Colorway.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/44191274180633) **Select Colorways** button. **Option** | **Transparent Background** | Save the image with a transparent background. **Save Separate Images** | Save the multi-view in individual images. **Save HTML File ** | A HTML file of the snapshot is also saved. **Open** | Open all the setting options in *.mvs file format. **Save** | Save all the setting options in *.mvs file format. **Reset** | Resets the options back to the program default settings. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to save 3D window snapshots in both single and multi-view formats, detailing customizable options for image size, orientation, resolution, and colorways.

title: Smart Arrangement
content: **Smart Arrangement** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wysSD11q5Qc \- Arrange the Patterns near their sewn pairs maintaining their drape. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Smart Arrangement.** \- The selected Pattern will be arranged next to the sewn pair without distortion of the drape.
content_description: Discover how to effectively use the Smart Arrangement feature in Clo3D to organize your garment patterns while preserving their drape.

title: Flip Horizontally (3D)
content: **Flip Horizontally** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cx7f8Ri-hQs \- Flip the selected Pattern horizontally. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select **Flip Horizontally.** \- The selected Pattern will flip horizontally, maintaining its drape
content_description: This webpage provides a step-by-step guide on how to flip a selected pattern horizontally in your 3D garment using the Clo3D software.

title: Pose (POS/HPOS) Open/Save
content: **Objective** Use this function to load an Avatar's Pose or location information. A variety of Avatar Poses are provided in the Library window. **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Open/ Save As ▶ **Pose/ Hand Pose (ver 7.1)** **Operation** **Open Pose** 1. Click the menu of the Location to open a Pose/Hand Pose. → Open Pose window appears. 2. Set the options and click the **OK** button. **Pose Only** | Applies the Pose Motion Data (Joint rotation) only, while maintaining the Avatar's Size. ---|--- **Pose & Joint Translation** | Applies the Avatar's Size, Pose, Motion Data (joint rotation) and Joint positions **Partial Pose (ver 7.1)** | Apply all pose files, or apply Hand Pose only. → If the pose is changed and the garments are put on, it is automatically simulated. **Save Pose** 1. Select the menu indicated. → The Save File window appears. → When there are more than two Avatars, select the appropriate one from the Save Pose window. 2. Designate the file name and the path and select the **Save** button. → The Pose(POS/HPOS) file is saved.
content_description: This web page provides instructions for loading and saving Avatar poses and location information using the Pose/Hand Pose feature.

title: Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)
content: **Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Hxe0BwEXzQo When you place fabric using Arrangement Points, it wraps around the avatar in a draped form. If you want to undo that and return the fabric to its original, flat position, use the Reset 3D Arrangement function. \- Use **Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/48000411030937)** when Garments are not properly draped after arranging them in the 3D window. \- Right-click on the Pattern to be re-arranged and select **Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected).** \- The selected Pattern will be re-arranged in the 3D window prior to the Simulation.
content_description: Learn how to effortlessly return your fabric to its original flat position using the "Reset 3D Arrangement (Selected)" feature in CLO 3D, ensuring perfect draping before simulation.

title: Garment File Save/Open
content: **List of Contents** Garment File Open Garment File Save Garment File **Garment File** \- The Garment file is composed with followings: 3D Garments, 2D Patterns, Colorways, Print Layout, and comments. Save above information along with 3D Garments as a .zpac file and re-open to edit. ** Open Garment File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jB27g_SM2I4 \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Open ▶ **Garment.** \- Locate the garment file and select **Open.** The selected garment file will load. **Save Garment File** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XE8fUfTfDzk \- Navigate to the Main Menu and select File ▶ Save As ▶ **Garment.** \- Assign the saving path and the file name, then click **Save.** Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to open and save garment files, including instructions for managing 3D garments, 2D patterns, and associated data.

title: Show UV Guide
content: **Show UV Guide** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LFVafDNnxyI \- Check the UV area before exporting the 3D Garment. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022677527/mceclip0.png) **Show** **UV Guide** tool from the 2D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to and select Main Menu ▶ Display ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ **Show** **UV Guide. ** \- When the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022677527/mceclip0.png) **Show UV Guide** tool is activated, the marquee box showing the UV area will appear.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on how to use the Show UV Guide tool in the 2D toolbar to check the UV area before exporting 3D garments, accompanied by a helpful YouTube video.

title: Show/Hide Avatar
content: **List of Contents** Avatar Display Icons Show Avatar Show Arrangement Point Show Bounding Volumes Show Avatar Measurements Show Avatar Tape Show 3D Lines **Avatar Display Icons** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XJUAbo31JBo \- Show or hide icons related to Avatars. \- Navigate to the 3D window and hover over the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu. ** ****Show Avatar** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G5GPqukCjbY \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022729208/mceclip6.png) **Show Avatar** icon to show or hide avatars from the 3D window. **Show Arrangement Point** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PsQrarfO6NU \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022667947/mceclip11.png) **Show Arrangement****Point** icon to show or hide arrangement points on Avatar. **Show Bounding Volumes** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dsQryIqd_3Q \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022729828/mceclip8.png) **Show Bounding Volumes** icon to show or hide bounding volumes on Avatar. **Show Avatar Measurements** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQWTd_EYHzM \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022729868/mceclip9.png) **Show Avatar Measurements** icon to show or hide measurements on Avatars.。 **Show Avatar Tape** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vUcr-hzgCyk \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022668107/mceclip12.png) **Show Avatar Tape** icon to show or hide Avatar Tapes on Avatars. **Show 3D Lines** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YechGNCPsbg \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022668127/mceclip14.png) **Show 3D Lines** icon to show or hide 3D lines drawn on Avatar. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore various tools and features for managing avatar visibility and measurements in the 3D window, complete with instructional videos for each option.

title: Grading
content: **List of Contents** Grading Create Size Group Add Size Delete **GradingYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PBTvcGPwdKA** \- Create and edit grading rules of a 3D Garment. \- Create Size Group Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ **+Add** Add Size Object Browser ▶ Grading Tab ▶ Size Group (Select the One to be Edited) ▶ **+** **Create Size GroupYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pl9_EgO3WYQ** \- Click the **+** button in the Object Browser’s Grading tab to add a new Size Group. \- By default, a new Size Group is added and one Base Size is created. \- Click the Size Group or the Size to view and edit its properties in the Property Editor. **Add SizeYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QEbdL_-LdhA** \- Click the **+** button next to each Size under a Size Group. \- A new Size is added and number is added at the end of the Size name in created order. \- Toggle on the check box in front to each Size to assign as Base Size. **Delete** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=b8VCgGfiMe4** \- Click the **Delete** icon on each Size’s right to delete the selected Size. \- Similarly, click the **Delete** icon on each Size Group’s right to delete the selected Size Group. \- When a Size Group is deleted, its Sizes under the Group are also deleted. ※ Note: * In order to paste in a grading value, the selected point must have a [Grading Size Group](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015578947). * Multiple grading values on multiple points cannot be pasted at once. However, one copied value can be pasted to multiple points. * Use the shortcuts: Crtl+Z, Ctrl+Y to undo or redo copy and paste. * Hide Patterns' grading rules using [Show/Hide Grading](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015876648). Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive instructions and video tutorials for managing grading rules, size groups, and sizes in a 3D garment design software.

title: Solidify
content: **List of Contents** Solidify Result of Solidify **Solidify** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jW7YiDEbfhU \- Fix the drape of the Pattern and maintain the shape while simulating. \- Use the Solidify function when creating a hat’s cap and a bra’s cup where Pattern shapes need to be fixed. \- Select the Patterns using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022683507/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool, right click, and select the **Solidify** option from the pop-up menu. \- Or, select the Patterns using the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022683507/mceclip0.png) **Transform Pattern** tool, navigate to the Property Editor and toggle on **Solidify** **Result of Solidify** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zkhlay2bIP8 \- The selected Pattern will maintain its drape. \- Set how strong Pattern will maintain its drape by adjusting the **Strengthen** option. \- The Selected Pattern will maintain its drape depending on the Strengthen setting when the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115022683567/mceclip1.png)**Simulation** is activated. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides a comprehensive guide on using the Solidify function in CLO 3D to enhance the drape and shape of patterns for fashion design projects, complete with instructional videos and step-by-step instructions.

title: Flatten
content: **List of Contents** Flatten Extract Pattern **Flatten YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KnZMw9OoIYs ** \- Extract Patterns based on the shapes on an Avatar, drawn with Line (Avatar.) \- Select the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021385127/mceclip0.png) **Flatten** tool from the 3D toolbar. \- Or, navigate to the Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Flatten.** ** Extract pattern** * **Extract Pattern YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BlkjbhN3gKY ** \- Select desired shapes on the Avatar to extract Patterns. \- Hover the mouse over the shapes to the extracted. \- The shape is highlighted in light-blue. \- Click all shapes to be extracted. \- Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- The selected shapes are extracted as Patterns and appear in both the 3D and 2D windows. \- The Default Fabric is automatically applied to Patterns that are extracted using the Flatten tool. \- Patterns adjacent to each other are sewn automatically. \- The Line (Avatar) remains on the Avatar. * **Extract Pattern by Selecting All YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=U6GFu_OYeOY ** \- Press Ctrl+A on the keyboard while the![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021385127/mceclip0.png) **Flatten** tool is selected, to extract all Patterns. \- All Patterns are selected. \- Hit the Enter key on the keyboard. \- All selected shapes are extracted as Patterns and appear in both of the 3D and 2D windows. \- The Default Fabric is automatically applied to Patterns that are extracted using the Flatten tool. \- Patterns adjacent to each other are sewn automatically. \- The Line (Avatar) remains on the Avatar. * **Cancel Selection** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bTXxAquN1GM * **Cancel Individually** \- Reselect the shape to cancel selection individually. * **Cancel All** \- To cancel all selections, hit the Esc key on the keyboard or Ctrl+Z at the same time. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides comprehensive instructions and video tutorials on using the Flatten and Extract Pattern tools in 3D garment design software.

title: AI Import of Patterns with Prints/Graphics Applied
content: **List of Contents** Import – Adobe (AI/PDF) Importing Patterns with Prints/Graphics **Import - Adobe (AI/PDF)YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K8XQettZT9I ** \- AI Patterns with graphics can be imported into CLO together, without having to import them separately. \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Import ▶ **ADOBE (AI/PDF).** **Importing Patterns with Prints/GraphicsYouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_NGcZtdRKc ** \- Navigate to Main Menu ▶ Import ▶ **ADOBE (AI/PDF)**. A file browser to select AI file will appear. Select the AI file to be imported. \- The Import AI/PDF pop-up window will appear. \- Toggle on **Import as Internal Shape** and **Import as Graphic.** \- Adjust related options in the Import AI/PDF pop-up window and select OK. \- The selected AI file will be imported with Prints/Graphics and each item can be edited individually. title: Emission Color
content: **Emission Color** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vtzyXCd0tLE \- Adjust the **Emission Color** to express retro-reflection and luminous materials which emit light by itself. \- Select the fabric item in the Object Browser to apply the Emission Color. \- Navigate to the Property Editor and select the color chip next to Material ▶ **Emission Color.** \- The Color window will appear allowing you to select the Emission Color. \- Click or type in desired values to RGB to apply the desired Emission Color to the fabric.

title: Reverse Arrange - Vertically
content: **Reverse Arrange - Vertically** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F743wtOp1Ac \- Reverse the Patterns vertically maintaining the curvature of the Patterns created when arranging them using the Arrangement Points. \- Choose the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021552387/mceclip0.png) **Select/Move** tool from the 3D toolbar and navigate to the 3D window. \- Right-click on the 3D Garment and select Reverse Arrange ▶ **Vertically.** \- The selected Pattern will flip vertically maintaining the curvature created when arranged via Arrangement Points.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide on how to reverse arrange patterns vertically in a 3D garment design while preserving their original curvature.

title: Quadrangular/Triangular Mesh
content: **Convert synchronized 3D Garments into quadrangular or triangular mesh structures.** **![29. Quad Mesh Improvement.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39597030520857)** **📝****Note:** Please refer below explanation on different usages of Quadrangular Mesh versus Triangular Mesh. As the program speed may differ due to the difference in their intrinsic characteristics, please select most appropriate Mesh Type based on your needs. To use our program most efficiently, however, we **strongly suggest** you to set all Pattern Mesh to Triangular when editing 3D Garments, and then change ONLY necessary Patterns' Mesh type to Quadrangular to complete the Garment. * **When to Use Triangular Mesh** : **All Cases,****** except for special cases needed to use Quadrangular Mesh. * **When to Use Quadrangular Mesh** : When a detail of 3D Garment needs to round smoothly such as shirts collar or piping. #### 1. Click the pattern in 2D or 3D window. 2. Change the Mesh Type to the Quad (Otimized) in the Property Editor.
content_description: This web page provides guidance on converting synchronized 3D garments into either quadrangular or triangular mesh structures, highlighting the optimal usage scenarios for each type to enhance garment design efficiency.

title: Edit 2D POM
content: **List of Contents** **Move** **Option** **Objective** Move Point/Segment or delete POM. [Watch Tutorial Video here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Cje0BzHiEAk) **Location**** ** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Point of Measure ▶**Edit Point of Measure** 2D Toolbar ▶ ![pommmm.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360040771653/pommmm.jpg) **Edit Point of Measure** **Operation ** **Move**** ** 1. Click on a point or a whole segment of the POM to be edited. → The point or segment is selected. → A pop-up menu appears when multiple POM points are overlapped. 2. Drag to the desired position. → The POM is moved to the position. → Similar to creating a POM, the line linking two Patterns is maintained as a link in the case of Group POM. 3. **When moving Segment and Curved points of a curved POM, hold down the D key on the keyboard and click-and-drag to move the selected points only. ** → The selected point is moved. **Option** 1. Right click on POM to set the options as needed. **Delete** | Delete the selected POM. ---|--- **Reverse** | Reverse the direction of the POM. **Segment Type/ Straight Type** | Apply as Pattern Outline or Straight Line. **X/ Y Dist Type** | Show the X/ Y axis distance based on the selected outline. **※ Note:****POM is moved when its intersected Pattern Oulines and Internal Lines are moved.**
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on how to move or delete Points of Measure (POM) within a 2D pattern, including step-by-step instructions and a tutorial video for enhanced understanding.

title: Alembic Import/Export
content: **List of Contents** Import Export #### Import/Export the object, cache, normal, and animation data contained within an Alembic file. #### #### **Import** 1. Click Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶**Alembic.** 2. Select the desired file and click **OK**. 3. Select the settings as needed and click **OK**. → The Alembic file is imported based on the setting. Option | **Description** ---|--- **FPS** | Sets the frame rate of the cache data. **Scale** | Input the scale directly or select from the available units. **Garment Position** | Moves the Garment to the location of the first frame. #### #### **Export** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ **Alembic.** 2. Designate the file saving path and the file name. Then, click **OK**. → The Export Alembic window appears. 3. Select the settings as needed and click **OK**. → The file is exported as an Alembic file based on the setting. Option | **Description** ---|--- **File** | Set the file type (OGAWA/HDF5) for export. **Object** | **Unweld** Exports the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into multiple objects. | ******Weld** Combines the Vertex (points of the mesh) of the parts of the pattern that are sewn together into one line into one point. **Weld Selected Pattern:** Weld based on the sewing line that connects the selected patterns **Thin** Ensures that the thickness will not be exported even if the rendering thickness value is increased beforehand. | **Thick** Exports a pattern with its rendering thickness values in its increased state. **Combined UV Coordinates:** Exports all Garment Pattern texture data fit to UV Coordinates ranging from 0 to 1. **Include Avatar Shape:** Save the Avatar as part of the file. **FPS** | Sets the frame rate of the cache data. **Step** | Adds/Subtracts frames for the recorded Animation according to the entered value. **Frame Relative Sample** | Sets the low and high values for frame relative sampling. **Scale** | Adjusts the scale of the file being exported when a value is entered or the desired unit from “Unit in file to import” is selected.
content_description: This web page provides detailed instructions for importing and exporting Alembic files, including settings for frame rate, scale, and garment positioning to optimize data management in your projects.

title: Does CLO have an online community?
content: **Yes, CLO has an active and supportive community!** The CLO community is made up of users from all over the world! From beginners to experienced professionals, who share knowledge, ask questions, and exchange tips about using CLO. ### **Where Can You Find the CLO Community?** * [**CONNECT** ](https://connect.clo-set.com/community)is CLO’s official community platform, where users can: * Interact, ask questions, and share their projects. * Offer or request personalized training. * Participate in **challenges.** * Explore inspiring **user stories.** * Browse or post on the **job board.** * Stay updated with events, news, and more. * **[CLO Discord](https://discord.com/invite/CujT8B5m5g)** offers real-time interaction between community members and CLO designers. It’s a place to: * Chat casually or get quick help. * Discuss tips and workflows. * Share feedback and feature requests. * Get support from experienced users and CLO staff. ### **Why Join the Community?** Being part of the CLO community helps you: * Learn faster from experienced users; * Connect with professionals in the digital fashion industry. * * * If you have any questions, please [Contact Us.](https://clo3d.com/en/support/contactus)
content_description: Join the global CLO community to connect, learn, and share insights with fellow users while enhancing your skills in digital fashion.

title: Gizmo Axis Setting
content: **Objective** There are three different Gizmo types in CLO. Select and utilize it as needed. ** Location** Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Gizmo** 3D Window ▶ Right-click (on the 3D window) ▶ **Gizmo** **Operation** 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Preferences ▶ **Gizmo** 3D Window ▶ Right-click (on the 3D window) ▶ **Gizmo ** 2. Select a desired **Gizmo**. 3. Select an object with **Select/Move Tool**. → The chosen type of **Gizmo** appears. 4. Click the axis of the **Gizmo** ▶ Drag it to the desired location. → The chosen object moves along with the Gizmo. **Screen Coordinate Gizmo** | Screen Coordinate Gizmo is based on the camera axis. Change the camera view in order to change the gizmo axis. Selected object moves along with the camera axis. ---|--- **Local Coordinate Gizmo** | Local Coordinate Gizmo axis is based on following the native direction of an object. Mainly usable when designing poses from the avatar's X-ray joint points. Selected object moves to native direction of an object. **World Coordinate Gizmo** | World Coordinate Gizmo is based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects. Selected object moves based on 3D space regardless of screens or objects.
content_description: Discover how to select and utilize different Gizmo types in CLO to effectively manipulate objects within the 3D environment.

title: 3D File (OBJ) Import/Export
content: **List of Contents** **Import/ Import (Add) OBJ** **Export OBJ** #### **Import OBJs as avatars, trims, and garments. ** **📝****Note:** 3D garments created in CLO can be exported as OBJ and compatible with other 3D software. An MTL file which saves material properties of the exported 3D garment is created at the time of OBJ export. #### #### **Import/ Import (Add) OBJ** 1. Click the Main Menu » File » Import/Import (Add) » **OBJ** 2. Select ta desired file and click **Open**. 3. Click**OK** after configuring options.** ** ** Object Type ** | ** Load as Avatar ** | Load an OBJ as an avatar to drape garments. **Automatically Add Arrangement Points -** Arrangement Points are automatically created based on the OBJ. **📝****Note:** Arrangement Points are properly created only when avatars are in either A or T-pose. ![00__1_.jpg](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/360003078687) ---|---|--- ** Load as Trim ** | Load an OBJ as a trim. OBJs imported as trims do not calculate collision. ** Load as Garment ** | Import and simulate an OBJ created in other 3D software such as Maya, 3ds Max, etc.). Toggle on **Trace 2D Patterns from UV Map** to automatically generate patterns based on the UV information. ** Load as Morph Target ** | Load an OBJ to morph already imported OBJ. Configure **Morphing Frame Count** to control morphing speed. Higher the value is, slower the morphing is. **📝****Note:** Morphing refers to a method to transform appearance of an OBJ according to another OBJ. For CLO avatars, users can modify the shape or pose by using **Avatar Size Editor** or **Show X-Ray Joints** features, but users cannot easily change imported OBJs created in other 3D software due to un-rigged joints or loss of joint information. Thus, users can utilize Load as Morph Target feature to change body shape or pose of the imported OBJ. However, to do so, users need two or more OBJ files with the identical mesh structure. ** Scale ** | Type in the Scale or select the desired unit. ** Axis Conversion ** | Invert each axis of the OBJ as needed. ** Translation ** | Locate the import position of the OBJ. Toggle on Align Bottom to Ground to surface the OBJ when it is located below the ground. #### #### **Export OBJ** 1. Click the Main Menu » File » Export » **OBJ/OBJ(Selected)** menu. 2. Locate the saving path and click **Save**. 3. Configure the options and click **OK**. **Object** **** **** **** | **Select All Patterns** | Select or deselect all Patterns. ---|---|--- ** Select All Avatars ** | Select or deselect all avatars/ objects. ** Select All Graphics/ Top-stitches ** | Select or deselect all graphics or top-stitches. Individual selection is available on the drop-down menu on the right. **Single Object/Multiple Objects** | Choose to export as a single object or multiple objects. **Unweld/ Weld** | Choose to export vertex (points of mesh) of sewn pattern parts as multiple objects or a single point. **Thin/ Thick** | Choose to export the object with thickness or not. **Combined UV Coordinates** | A combined UV coordinates is also exported. **Include Internal Shape** | Export with internal line and/or shape information . **Scale** | Scale the exported object's size. **Axis Conversion** | Change directions of object's each axis. **File** | **Save Colorway** | Export colorway along with the *.obj file. **Maintain Individual Texture Image Coordinates** | Each colorway is exported individually as *.obj and *.mtl files. **Share Texture Image Coordinates** | All colorways are exported as a single *.obj and as many *.mtl files as colorways. **Save with Absolute Texture Image File Path ** | Export OBJ to the original file's saving path. **📝****Note:** When there is not image file at the original path, it may get lost as this option only saves the path. **Save with Texture Files (ZIP)** | Export OBJs along with textures. **Diffuse Color Combined on Texture** | When color is applied to the texture, the color is blended into the texture when exporting. **Exclude Ambient Map & Color (Modo)** | Ambient Map and color are excluded when exporting. **Save with Transparency Map Extracted from Diffuse Map** | Alpha Map is included when exporting. **Save with Meta Data(XML)** | Exports garment's patter(Mesh), physical property and sewing information as Meta Data. Combine and save garment's texture image and color as a single image. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This webpage provides comprehensive guidance on importing and exporting OBJ files for 3D garments, avatars, and trims, facilitating seamless integration with various 3D software.

title: Automatic Rigging & Converter
content: Conver to Avatar Custom Rigging **Objective** Add joints or convert user data to CLO avatars and use CLO Avatar Editor. YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LvIJPBT7EOo ** Location** Main Menu ▶Avatar ▶ **Auto Convert to Avatar** ** Operation** **Convert to Avatar** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated. → Auto Convert to Avatar pop-up menu appears. → The Auto Avatar Converter deletes all avatars in the 3D window. 2. After setting the options below, click the Convert button. **Menu** | **Description** ---|--- **Open the file to be converted** | Click the Open button on the right to load 3D dummy and scan files to be rigged and converted. **※ Note:** The Daz3D Genesis 8 version of the file is automatically recognized and converted into each high-quality avatar and accessory. The converted accessories are compatible with avatars of the same version and gender.(ver 7.3**[![Youtube_Icon__1_.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/35994900272793)](https://youtu.be/WRkb4MR0dP0?si=He--Y05xs3Pr2aki&t=1746)**) **Gender** | Set the gender of the avatar to be converted **Converting Option** | Convert an avatar automatically or [Maintain Custom Rig.](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360055227373-%EC%9E%90%EB%8F%99-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%EB%A6%AC%EA%B9%85-%EB%B3%80%ED%99%98-ver-6-0-#Click1) **Converted Output (AVT)** | **CLO Skin Style ** The body shape of the original file is maintained and only the appearance is converted to a CLO avatar and joint points are added. | **※ Note:** When converting to the avatar, size editing is not possible. The CLO Avatar Size Editor automatically fits into a realistic body shape based on thousands of actual scanned data so it cannot keep the body shape of the original file. **Rigging only** Only the joint points are added while maintaining both the body shape and appearance of the original file.** ** **Convert to[size editable avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360013257553--Size-Editor-Adjust-Avatar-Size-ver5-0-0-and-Above-) **Change the CLO avatar body shape so that the size can be edited while maintaining the appearance of the file to be converted and add joint points. **※Note: **The conversion options below can be multi-selected and are compatible with the CLO avatar pose/motion provided in the Library after conversion. **Save** | Click the Save button on the right and specify the path to save the converted avatar file. → The file will be converted to an avatar with the options users set which may take 5-10 minutes. **Custom Rigging** * **Opacity Setting** Change the opacity of the garment to make it easier to see the avatar. 1. 3D Tool Bar ▶ Select the file to convert with **Select/Move Tool**. 2. Property Editor ▶ Material (Selected) ▶ Basic Parameters ▶ Set **the opacity** to **50**. 3. Change the color of the file as required. * **Adjust Whole Body** [Main Menu ▶ Avatar ▶ Avatar Size Editor](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/360013257553-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%EC%82%AC%EC%9D%B4%EC%A6%88-%EC%A1%B0%EC%A0%88) Align the CLO avatar with the Custom avatar by adjusting the below 3 points of measurement. * Align the height of the shoulder and inseam. Choose one of the cases applicable. **A****.** When using Total Height Click the up/down triangle button to the right of the Total Height number box to increase or decrease the avatar's height so the shoulder line is the same on both avatars. The shoulder shape of the Custom Avatar and the CLO avatar are different, so it is not necessary to perfectly match the shoulder position. Just using the triangle button ![mceclip1.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266924313) to align with a similar shoulder line is sufficient, and you do not need to manually enter a precise value to align. Some errors are automatically adjusted during conversion. ![mceclip2.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403260258073) **B.** When using HPS Height and Inseam If the inseam height difference is too large when adjusting the shoulder line through Total Height, the shoulder line is adjusted according to the inseam measurement. After fixing, adjust the Inseam to fit. At this time, change the unnaturally deformed upper body naturally by adjusting the height of the CF/CB Neck to Waist. **B-1)** Set the Height type to the HPS Height. **B-2)** Align the shoulder height using the up/under triangle button in the input box. **B-3)** Details ▶ Inseam Height align the inseam height using the up/under triangle button. ![mceclip3.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266934169) As the width of the adjustment of the inseam increases, the length of the upper body changes according to the Inseam. Since the CF/CB Neck to Waist value that controls the length of the upper body is fixed, the body shape may change unnaturally. In this case, it can be reflected in the result, so it is important to match the face and body shape of the avatars naturally. Recover naturally by following the method below. * **B-4)** Details ▶ CF Neck to Waist/CB Neck to Waist. Press the triangle button on the right side of the number box in the opposite direction you pressed in the inseam to adjust the body shape until it looks natural. (e.g, if the length of the Inseam is shortened, the lengths of the two lower upper body lengths will be increased.) Normally, if you press the CF and CB triangle buttons the same number of times, the body shape is adjusted with a balanced front/back. ![mceclip4.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403260267033) * Match the arm length 1. Check the arm length once you adjust the shoulder height and the inseam. 2. If the lengths to the wrist are different, click the up/down triangle button to the right of the CF Neck to Wrist number box to match the length to the avatar's wrist. ![mceclip5.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266946969) * **Adjusting pose** [Avatar Display in the 3D window ▶ Show X-Ray Joints](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000406887-%EC%95%84%EB%B0%94%ED%83%80-%ED%8F%AC%EC%A6%88-%EB%B3%80%EA%B2%BD) Match the pose and the joint points of the CLO avatar according to the pose of the Custom Avatar so that the two avatars overlap each other. Rotate the joints to make both avatars overlap. **※Note:** If you can't see the overlapped avatars well when Show X-Ray Joints in on, click the joint and press Shift+X to keep using the Gizmo to adjust the joints with the textured avatar. To utilize the above method, you need to change the default gizmo of the 3D window to [Local Coordinate](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000415867-%EA%B8%B0%EC%A6%88%EB%AA%A8-%EC%B6%95-%EB%B3%80%EA%B2%BD), which is the same as the joint point view mode. * Fitting the lower body 1. Click the avatar's center joint point (purple) to bring up the gizmo and adjust the front/back position so the hips of the two avatars overlap. 2. Click the hip joint to check both the front and the side, and align the ankles of the two avatars so that they overlap. 3. Click the ankle point to adjust the insteps of the two avatars to overlap. * Fitting the upper body 1. Click the waist joint and rotate it from the side until the front of the avatar's neck and shoulders are overlapped. If you can't hit it all at once, align the shoulders first, then rotate the joint point on the side where the neck starts to align the front of the neck. ![mceclip6.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266956057) 2. Rotate the shoulder point to adjust the cuff to overlap. If it is not possible to align the wrist joint with the shoulder joint point, **align** the elbow joint first, then **rotate** the elbow joint to align the wrist joint. 3. Click the wrist joint point to align the back of the hand. First, align the first finger joints/knuckle placements If the length of your finger is different, adjust the value of “Avatar Size Editing Window ▶ Details ▶ Arm ▶ Hand” to match the length. ![mceclip7.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266960793) 4. Click the joint point that is connected to the finger near the wrist joint point to align the gap between the fingers. ![mceclip8.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266964505) 5. Click the joint point where the finger starts to overlap the finger to the end. Rather than mesh the fingers of the two avatars, focus on locating the joint points at the appropriate places on the Custom avatar. ![mceclip9.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/4403266968473)
content_description: The "Convert to Avatar Custom Rigging" page guides users through the process of transforming 3D dummy and scan files into customized CLO avatars with added joint points, utilizing the CLO Avatar Editor for enhanced rigging and compatibility.

title: Human IK – Edit Full Body/ Edit Body Part
content: **Human IK - Edit Full Body/Edit Body Part ** \- Decide how to move and rotate Avatar joints. Only one option can be used at a time. * **Edit Full Body YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cSGxKH9NXGY \- **When moving and rotating a single joint, all others joints will be modified as well to create an organic pose. * **Edit Body Part ** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=akpCa7X1MYc \- When moving and rotating a single joint, only directly connected joints will be modified.
content_description: Explore the Human IK tool to seamlessly edit full body poses or individual body parts of your avatar, enhancing movement with intuitive joint manipulation.

title: Offset Avatar Joint
content: ## **New in 2024.2** #### **Adjust avatar joint offsets for various body shapes using just a single motion file** **![21. Avatar Joint Offset.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39598607549081)** **📝****Note:** This can be helpful when the same avatar has varying body shapes. For example, the offset can be adjusted to correct the distance between the hands and hips in a motion when it does not align due to the avatar's body shape. #### 1. Open the Motion file in Animation Mode. 2. Right-click on the animation layer corresponding to the motion file, and click the**Offset Joint** menu. 3. Click on the Joint. 4. Rotate directly with the gizmo or adjust each axis in the Offset Joint window. → The joint offset is applied to the motion where you right-clicked.
content_description: Discover how to easily adjust avatar joint offsets for various body shapes in CLO 2024.2 using a single motion file to ensure accurate alignment during animations.

Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Window ▶ Right-click Pop-up Menu (On Avatar) ▶ **Reset Joints** → Avatar's joints reset.

title: Human IK
content: **List of Contents** Definition of Human IK Human IK Use Human IK ** Definition of Human IK** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dtYCS6fOjIs \- Avatar joints are organically linked that joints move naturally when modifying one particular joint, allowing easier pose modification process. ** Human IK** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=i0B1d2VVvOQ \- Hover over the second icon in the Vertical View Toggle Menu to view Avatar Display options. \- Select the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021444148/mceclip1.png) **Show X-ray Joints** icon. \- The Human IK window will appear on the right top corner of the 3D window. **Use Human IK** **YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gtJVFyh8EUI ** * **Move Joints** \- Avatar joints will appear in yellow-green on the Avatar’s elbows, knees, and more. \- Click and drag the desired Avatar joint to modify the pose. * **Rotate Joints** \- When the Avatar joint is clicked once, the **Gizmo** tool will appear. \- Use the circles of the **Gizmo** tool to rotate joint and modify the pose. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: Explore the functionality and usage of Human IK for natural avatar joint manipulation and pose modification through informative videos and detailed instructions.

title: Adjust Avatar Joints
content: #### **List of Contents** Show Avatar Joints FK (Forward Kinematics) IK (Inverse Kinematics) Set Joint Size #### **Change the avatar pose by moving and rotating the avatar joint ** #### #### **Show Avatar Joints** 1. Hover over the ![Avatar Main Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38295892402329) **Avatar Display** in the 3D window, then click the ![Avatar Sub Avatar Joints Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38295863753497)**Show Avatar Joints**. #### #### **FK (Forward Kinematics)** You can adjust each joint individually to fine-tune the pose. 1. Use the[ Gizmo](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/ko/articles/115000513928-%EA%B8%B0%EC%A6%88%EB%AA%A8%EB%A1%9C-%EC%9D%B4%EB%8F%99-%EB%B0%8F-%ED%9A%8C%EC%A0%84) to adjust the position and rotation by clicking on the joint. #### #### **IK (Inverse Kinematics)** You can adjust the specific joint, and the organically linked joints are automatically calculated to easily express realistic pose. 1. Change the mode to**IK** in Avatar Joint window. 2. Set the options as needed. Option | **Description** ---|--- **Full Body** | When a single joint is modified, it affects all other joints which are organically linked to the single joint. **Body Part** | When a single joint is modified, only directly connected joints are modified. **Constrain Joint Translation** | Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other moving joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may move slightly. **Constrain Joint Rotation** | Activate the option to prevent unwanted movement of the selected joint caused by other rotating joints. However, for natural modification of the Avatar, the constrained joint may rotate slightly. 3. Use the Gizmo to adjust the position and rotation by clicking on the joint. _* If the joints and axes of the avatar are symmetrical, you can adjust the joints symmetrically by clicking the symmetric button next to the Gizmo. _ **📝****Note:** * Human IK created in other 3D software is not compatible with CLO. * To import avatars created in other 3D software, the avatar must have the same bone structure and names. * To refer to CLO avatars' bone structures and names, please download the files below. #### #### ![Label_Final.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38305848749081) #### **Set Joint Size** Set the joint size smaller to make selection easier on avatars with a lot of joints. ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/38306484487193) 1. Enter the size in the Avatar Joint window. #### Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for manipulating avatar joints using Forward and Inverse Kinematics to customize poses effectively in a 3D environment.

title: Human IK – Constrain Joint Rotation
content: **Human IK - Constrain Joint Rotation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BHU-Ch7uC8I \- Fix the selected joint to minimize the modification when other joints are rotated. \- For organic movement, the selected joint may not completely be constrained. \- Select the Avatar joint to be constrained and click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021387107/mceclip0.png) **Constrain Joint Rotation** icon from the Human IK window. \- The constrained joint will turn grey and the alphabet R will hover over the joint.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the Human IK feature to constrain joint rotation for enhanced control and organic movement in character animation.

title: Human IK – Constrain Joint Translation
content: **Human IK - Constrain Joint Translation** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3KHlVviBtB8 \- Fix the selected joint to minimize the modification when other joints are moved. \- For organic movement, the selected joint may not completely be constrained. \- Select the Avatar joint to be constrained and click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021387127/mceclip0.png) **Constrain Joint Translation** icon from the Human IK window. \- The constrained joint will turn grey and the alphabet T will hover over the joint.
content_description: This web page provides a concise guide on using the Human IK feature to constrain joint translation for optimal organic movement in character animation.

title: Human IK – Show Human IK Joint
content: **Human IK - Show Human IK Joint** YouTube Video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TG0ucloN_Xg \- Link and move joints organically. -The ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021387367/mceclip0.png) **Show Human IK Joint** is activated by default when the **Show X-Ray Joints** icon is selected. \- Click the ![](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/115021387367/mceclip0.png) Show Human IK Joint to deactivate the function. When the **Human IK** is deactivated, each joint will move separately.
content_description: Explore how to organically link and move joints in Human IK by watching our tutorial video and learning about the Show Human IK Joint feature.

title: Grading Review
content: **List of Contents** Generate Data for Review Open Layout Setting Full Screen Save Image #### **All Grading Sizes of Garments and Avatars can be compared on one screen.** **Grading Review is activated based on the simulated results for each grading size. ** #### #### ******Generate Data for Review** 1. Click the Pair Avatar tab and click the **Update** after [creating](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015578947-Add-Apply-Grading) and [editing](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115015798567-Edit-Grading) the grading. → The 3D window's avatar is basically applied to all sizes. → If there are two or more size groups, they are combined based on the base size. 2. [Change the avatar for each grading size](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/360055935233-Pair-Avatar-for-Grading-Size-ver-6-0-) as needed. 3. Click the checkbox to the right of each size item and simulate. → The simulation result of the garment of the size on the avatar is automatically saved. → After simulation for each size, if the mesh of the pattern is changed due to work such as pattern correction, simulation must be performed again. #### #### ******Open** 1. Click the Main Menu ▶ Production ▶ **Grading Review.** 2. If re-simulation is required, click the ![Simulation Normal On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942141269017)**simulation** at the top left of each size. 3. Move, zoom and rotate the view of the 3D window. 4. Click the icon at the top to set [the rendering status of the garment and avatar](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/en-us/articles/115001025968-3D-Window-Display-Icons-). ![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942125826585) ### ![Label.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/39592363602457) Show or hide the**Pressure map** in the Grading Review. _****_ 1. Click and hold the ![Fit Maps Off Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942325625881)**Fit Maps** tool for more than 2 seconds, then click the ![Fit Maps Pressure Map Hover.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942325637145)**Pressure Map. ** 2. Re-simulate to get the result. #### #### ******Layout Setting** 1. Enter the width and height directly to adjust the size of each 3D window. 2. Click the![Review Warp On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942141294873)**Layout** to set the 3D window layout. **Options** | **Description** ---|--- **Wrap** | The 3D windows will be wrapped and aligned according to the width of the Grading Review window **Horizontal** | Align the 3D windows horizontally. **Vertical** | Align the 3D windows vertically. **Panoramic**** **| All grading sizes can be checked and compared at one in a single 3D window. **Rotation** | Each grading size rotates on the X-axis. **Distance** | The Space for each grading size is adjusted 3. Click the ![Review Reset Layout On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942125896857)**Reset Layout** to return to the initial layout. #### #### ******Full Screen** 1. Click the![Review Full Screen On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942125903769)**Full Screen.** 2. Press the ESC key on your keyboard to exit Full Screen. #### #### ******Save Image** 1. Click the ![Review Save On.png](https://support.clo3d.com/hc/article_attachments/37942141309593)**Save** and specify a name and path. 2. Check the option to save Transparent Background and Separate Images and click the 'Save'. #### **📝****Note****:** Right-click on the screen▶ if you click the Hide Grading Size, the hidden size disappears in the 3D window. Go back to the List of Contents
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide for efficiently reviewing and simulating garment grading sizes and avatars in a 3D environment.
